ruleName: Ball rolls into your own footprints
title: Ball Rolls Back Into Your Footprints in Bunker
question: After playing a shot from a bunker, your ball rolls back and comes to rest in the footprints you made. What are your options?

choices.text: Smooth out the footprints before your next shot
Play the ball as it lies or declare it unplayable
Move the ball to a nicer patch of sand

explanation: You must play the ball as it lies, even if it is in your own footprints, unless you declare the ball unplayable under the rules.

juniorVersion.title: Your Ball Stops in Your Own Footprints in the Sand
juniorVersion.question: You hit your golf ball from the bunker and it rolls back into the marks your feet made in the sand. What should you do?

choices.text: Smooth the sand where your ball stopped before you hit
Pick up your ball and put it somewhere else in the bunker for free
Hit the ball from the spot where it is, or say it is unplayable
Move your ball to a spot with smoother sand

juniorVersion.explanation: You have to play your ball from the footprints, or you can say it is unplayable and follow those rules. You cannot smooth the sand or move the ball to a nicer spot.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A sandy area on the golf course, sometimes called a sand trap.
When you decide your ball is too hard to play, you can choose to take a penalty and drop it somewhere else by the rules.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Ask the child to show how they would play a shot from rough sand, and talk about why the rule says to leave the sand how it is.
likelyMisconceptions: Children might think it’s okay to smooth the sand before hitting the next shot.
They might believe they can always move their ball to a better spot in the bunker without penalty.
